title: Twisted Mirror Path Count
summary: Given an m x n grid with cells either empty (0) or containing a mirror (1), a robot starts at (0, 0) and aims to reach (m - 1, n - 1) by moving only right or down.
statement: Given an m x n grid with cells either empty (0) or containing a mirror (1), a robot starts at (0, 0) and aims to reach (m - 1, n - 1) by moving only right or down. When the robot encounters a mirror, it is reflected: right into a mirror turns it down, and down into a mirror turns it right. If a reflection would move the robot out of bounds, the path is invalid. Count the number of unique valid paths, modulo 10^9 + 7, considering reflections within mirror cells.
constraints: Both dimensions are between two and 500; start and finish are empty.
Entering a mirror turns rightward motion down and downward motion right, chaining immediately.
hints: At a mirror, the outgoing direction depends on the direction used to enter, so retain two arrival counts.
Scan cells topologically with separate right-arrival and down-arrival DP tables.
Empty cells send their total both ways; mirrors send right arrivals down and down arrivals right.
Every move increases a coordinate, so row-major propagation counts each choice sequence once and chained mirrors follow automatically.
editorial: Every move increases a coordinate, so row-major propagation counts each choice sequence once and chained mirrors follow automatically.

tests.explanation: Five choice sequences reach the finish after applying mirror turns.
The ordinary right-down and down-right paths both remain valid.
